title: Chapter 275: The Ghost in His Heart! [2 in 1]
html:
The sender apparently had not expected such a direct reply. Ten seconds passed before a new message arrived. “I’m hiding in the wardrobe in Room 3239. Things are moving around me.”

“Can you describe their size and shape?” Too impatient to type, Chen Ge sent a voice message.

“I can’t see clearly. It’s too dark, but I can feel them nearby.”

“You have your phone. Why not switch on the flashlight and look?”

“I will be discovered.”

“Then how did you enter Room 3239? Do you have a key?”

“No. The door was open, so I slipped inside.”

“What happened to Uncle Wong?”

“Uncle Wong?”

Until then, replies had come almost instantly. The screen showed that the other party was typing, yet no message appeared.

Did I spoil the conversation?After waiting without success, Chen Ge sent ‘Xiao Gu’ another message. “Are you there?”

By the time the elevator reached the twenty-third floor, he had sent the question thirteen times.

“Are you there?”

As he prepared to send a fourteenth, Chen Ge discovered that the account had blocked him. You harassed me first, yet you’re the one blocking me. What is wrong with you?

He stepped from the elevator and pressed the recorder’s play button.

The bloodstained tape began to turn. Chen Ge narrowed his eyes, minimizing the darkness’s effect on his vision. Don’t worry. I’m here to correct your behavior.

Every nerve tightened. Keeping close to the wall, Chen Ge advanced slowly down the corridor.

After reading the message, Xiao Jia lost control and bit his partner. The hidden ghost can influence minds. The Ghost Stories Society’s blood face possessed a similar ability, but it needed proximity and had to copy its target’s features before the power worked.

This is a specialized ghost. Creatures with unusual abilities, like the Pen Spirit, are normally poor at direct combat.

Chen Ge had brought neither Doctor Skull-cracker’s hammer nor the cleaver. One hand closed around the ballpoint pen in his pocket, while the other remained against the wall. Any door ahead might open without warning and disgorge a ghost. Counting apartment numbers, he soon reached Room 3239. The handle refused to turn.

This should be it.He knocked. “Is anyone there?”

Shrill static hissed from the bloodstained tape, as though Xu Yin were warning him. Chen Ge knocked several more times. To his surprise, a man finally answered from inside. “Yes, I’m here! Who is disturbing people at this hour? What do you want?”

Someone actually lives here?Chen Ge was more surprised than the resident. Either the Ghost Stories Society controlled the man, or the man belonged to it. Anxiety pulled his senses taut.

Fang Hwa Apartments used double-layer doors. The inner door opened, revealing a man roughly 1.7 meters tall. He regarded Chen Ge coldly. “What do you want?”

“I’m assisting the police with a fugitive search. Additional officers will arrive shortly.” Chen Ge perfectly imitated Captain Yan’s tone and manner.

“Another fugitive?” The man’s expression hardened, his brows drawing together.

“Honey, what’s wrong?” A woman around thirty emerged from the living room.

“There’s another fugitive apparently.”

“Didn’t a fugitive enter this complex only a few days ago? This place is dangerous. How many times must this happen?” Her voice sharpened. “I told you we should move, but you refuse to listen!”

“Move? Where exactly do you expect us to go?” The man’s temper flared, and neither side yielded. Chen Ge observed their argument dispassionately. He could not confirm they belonged to the Ghost Stories Society, but instinct warned him that something was wrong.

People in a real argument meet each other’s eyes. Emotion also drives unconscious gestures, yet these two move stiffly and avoid looking directly at one another. Are they restraining themselves because I’m here, or is the entire quarrel staged?After a while, the woman abandoned her husband at the door and strode back inside.

The man seemed to contain a furnace of anger, and his manner toward Chen Ge turned openly hostile. “We live here. We haven’t seen a fugitive or heard anything strange. Go disturb someone else.”

No normal resident would invite a stranger inside after midnight, so Chen Ge had expected the refusal. Had the man welcomed an inspection, that would have been far more suspicious.

“I only have a few questions.” Chen Ge indicated the surrounding doors. “Do you know your neighbors?”

“The neighboring apartments are vacant. A single man lives across from us. He arrived a month or two ago and rarely comes out, so I know little about him.”

“When was the last time you saw him?”

“Probably Wednesday night. I worked three hours late and met him near the elevator.”

“Wednesday night? Near the elevator?” Chen Ge immediately connected the neighbor to the Ghost Stories Society. “Do you know his name?”

“No idea.” The man slammed the door, and the impact echoed down the corridor. Chen Ge turned toward the apartment opposite Room 3239.

“Is a Ghost Stories Society member hiding here?” Suspicion filled his gaze. The couple had looked normal yet ‘accidentally’ revealed two critical details—Wednesday and the elevator. Only society members should know them. Did they reveal those clues deliberately to lure me across the hall?

Coincidence or trap, Chen Ge could not tell. The black phone had taught him increasing caution. His right hand closed around the ballpoint pen while his left turned the handle. The door opened slowly.

Unlocked?Chen Ge immediately stepped back. This apartment, not Room 3239, was the true trap. The instant he released the handle, a child-sized hand slick with blood shot through the gap.

It missed him by centimeters.

What was that?!

The door creaked wider. A little boy climbed through, his limbs tiny, his head enormous, and his face purple from asphyxiation.

What made Chen Ge’s heart convulse was the boy’s red shirt.

Twisted lips parted over uneven teeth. The boy appeared to smile.

“Daddy killed us and placed us inside the door.

“Big brother is hiding behind the door.

“And he told me to hide in front of the door.”

As the boy finished, another misshapen head emerged from the apartment. Its face was bloated, its eyes nearly bursting from their sockets.

“Daddy killed us and placed us inside the door.

“Little brother is hiding in front of the door.

“And he told me to hide behind the door.”

Wearing curious expressions, both boys climbed into the corridor and faced Chen Ge, one before the doorway and one behind it. Fresh blood trickled from their bodies and became vessels that crept across floor and walls like millipedes. The corridor had turned deadly, yet the Ghost Stories Society’s trap was still unfolding.

A white shadow crawled from Room 3239—the same creature that had escaped the woman who murdered Xu Yin. Only a third of its body remained. It tried to flee across the carpet of blood vessels, but something dragged it back inside, followed by the sound of chewing.

More monsters are inside that room?Unfortunately, he was right. A blood-vessel-covered hand reached out. It was human-sized but terribly burned, with no fingerprints remaining.

The air seemed to congeal as the smell of blood thickened. The hand rested on one boy’s head like a loving father tousling his child’s hair. “He found you. Now it is your turn to find him.”

The man’s voice was raw and guttural, as though corrosive chemicals had destroyed his throat. The sound alone made Chen Ge’s skin crawl. Both boys in red smiled with sudden delight and answered together, “Yes, Father.”

The broken-faced boys rushed Chen Ge. Xu Yin could barely withstand one Red Specter, much less two. A pressure unlike anything Chen Ge had felt before crushed down upon him. Without hesitation, he shouted the name written on the cursed love letter. “Zhang Ya!”

Like a drop striking a bottomless well, ripples spread through Chen Ge’s shadow. The crawling vessels froze. Even the fingerprintless hand outside the door shuddered. Black hair surged from Chen Ge’s shadow in waves, crashing against both walls and violently crushing every vessel reaching for him.

The temperature on the twenty-third floor plummeted. Zhang Ya’s beautiful face appeared behind Chen Ge. Beneath that bone-chilling presence burned a soul of fierce passion.

“This is the ghost in your heart?” The man slowly emerged from behind the door. He wore a loose red jacket and a mask that did little to conceal his utterly ruined face.

“Zhang Ya, be careful!” Chen Ge retreated from the battlefield; in a clash between Red Specters, he could contribute nothing. His warning went unanswered, though Zhang Ya would never have listened regardless.

Zhang Ya wasted no time on words or tests. Resentment filled her eyes, and her black hair rose like a tidal wave, scoring the walls as it rushed toward the boys.

Blood vessels intertwined with black hair, the opposing forces crashing together like waves. Sheltered behind Zhang Ya, Chen Ge considered the enemy’s identity.

The man controlling those boys must be Patient 10 from the Third Sick Hall.His face and body were burned, and even his fingerprints had vanished—perfectly matching Patient 10’s description.The Haunted House recreated every sickroom from the Third Sick Hall, and Room 10’s walls recorded its occupant’s history. An accident killed both of his children, and unbearable guilt and trauma shattered his mind.

Every detail matched. Chen Ge had never expected to face the Third Sick Hall’s most terrifying patient that night.

He had underestimated the Ghost Stories Society’s determination to kill him. It had probably devised this plan immediately after losing contact with Kong Xiangming and Wei Wu. With a strategist as intelligent as Wu Fei, the society would not repeat the same mistake. It might have deployed every remaining member tonight.

Even Zhang Ya’s presence offered little reassurance. Patient 10 alone controlled two Red Specters, and the Ghost Stories Society still had six other members.

BANG!

Blood vessels burst apart. Zhang Ya’s hair coiled around one boy’s neck and slammed him into the floor. Strangely, he showed no pain; his misshapen face continued smiling. “Big brother, I can’t breathe.”

His crooked head swelled as vessels surfaced across his face, the noose of black hair threatening to burst his skull.

Yet neither the other Red Specter nor the man by the door attempted to help. Instead, the man ordered the older brother to bypass Zhang Ya and attack Chen Ge.

Black hair engulfed the younger brother. After a bloodcurdling scream, vessels seeped through the strands rather than being absorbed. They gathered nearby and slowly formed another boy. His head was smaller and his red shirt paler, but otherwise he appeared unchanged.

“What are you two waiting for?” the ruined man growled, pain and anger mingling in his voice.

“We wanted to wait until the situation stabilized. The ghost in his heart is clearly stronger than most.” The door to Room 3239 opened, and the supposed couple emerged. A thin monster stood on the husband’s shoulders, while the wife walked backward, revealing the blood face smiling from her skull.

They stepped out laughing, already certain of victory. The moment the door opened, however, black hair struck and wrapped around their bodies like a giant python.

Zhang Ya was facing four Baleful Specters at once—and two were Red Specters.

The man and woman exchanged a glance, each seeing fear, shock, and despair reflected in the other’s eyes.

“Didn’t you say you could restrain the monster attached to him?” the woman screamed. Before she could say more, black hair flooded every opening in the blood face.

The man screamed too. His thin monster tried to withdraw into his body, but black hair tightened around it and slowly dragged it free.

“One against four?” The ruined man slowly clenched his burned hand. He had considered the plan perfect, yet something unforeseen had overturned it.

Black hair flowed like a river through the blood-red world. Her red dress fluttering, Zhang Ya stood silently in the corridor. At the man’s voice, she slowly drew her gaze away from Chen Ge.

When she noticed the ruined man, her eyes brightened as though she had discovered a new toy.
